subject: Re: MAP: evaluation hypothesis, acceptance heuristics & close runbook
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Sanders <alex.s@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: evaluation hypothesis, acceptance heuristics & close runbook

Alex —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Attached is a first-pass MAP and a short CSV of proposed evaluation scenarios (attached: MAP-v1-mutual-action-plan.pdf, eval-test-scenarios.csv). High level — we want the MAP to be a lightweight operational contract that lets your engineering and procurement teams run a short, deterministic evaluation and have a clear path to close.

What I want to align on from Redwood's side:
- Acceptance heuristics (what counts as a successful eval vs. a minor regression)
- Exit gates (hard failures that would stop a go/no-go)
- A minimal set of acceptance tests (functional smoke + SLO verification + security checklist)
- Timeline and owners so we can hit your quarter close date

A few concrete proposals (please review and push back):
1) Hypothesis: Replacing the existing rule-based summarizer with Redwood inference will increase QA triage throughput by 30% while keeping semantic recall >= 95% (measured on your 500-case seed set).
2) Must-pass acceptance heuristics:
   - Core correctness: semantic recall >= 95% (F1-style) across seed set
   - Latency: p95 generation < 500ms for target prompt distribution
   - Safety: no high-severity hallucination in top-5 sampled outputs on 50 adversarial prompts
3) Exit gates (stop conditions):
   - Any data exfiltration finding in the security review
   - Mean latency > 1s on baseline traffic for 30+ minutes during a controlled run
   - Regression in semantic recall > 6 percentage points vs baseline
4) Acceptance tests (owner in parentheses):
   - Functional smoke: 100 sample prompts, pass if recall >= 95% (Acme eng / Redwood eng)
   - Load canary: 10k tokens/min sustained for 30 minutes, measure p50/p95 (Redwood infra)

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the clear write-up. A couple quick questions from our side: 

1) On latency: our current target for interactive triage is p95 < 300ms. Can you run a head-to-head with our current baseline or do you expect p95 < 500ms is a realistic target for the first pass?
2) For the safety checks — can you share the rubric you use to classify "high-severity hallucination"? We need that to satisfy our risk team.
3) Procurement wants to know what evidence they'll see during the trial to greenlight capacity reservations (they prefer quantitative dashboards + sample logs).

Also — what would a 3-week accelerated evaluation look like (we'd like to try to compress if possible).

Best,
Alex

Subject: Re: MAP: evaluation hypothesis, acceptance heuristics & close runbook

Alex —

Quick answers inline and a tighter 3-week plan below. (Forwarded: your note is quoted at the bottom.)

Latency: our recommended first-pass is p95 < 500ms on a medium instance profile; hitting p95 < 300ms is achievable with a short tuning pass (quantization profile + smaller context window) for interactive workloads. Karthik, I tagged you to propose the tuning steps.

Safety rubric: attached in the MAP PDF is a short classification matrix we use: "High severity" = hallucination that would change clinical decision or cause PHI leakage. We'll include examples and labeling guidance so your risk team can reproduce.

Procurement evidence: we will provide a shared dashboard (metrics + per-request latency histograms), a GPT-style sample log (redacted), and a reproducible smoke-run report (artifact). Links to sample artifacts will be in the Drive folder.

Proposed 3-week accelerated run (owners in parens):
Week 0 (prep — 2 business days): test account, seed data ingest, onboarding checklist (Redwood eng / Acme eng)
Week 1 (functional + safety): run functional smoke (100 prompts), adversarial safety set, initial metrics capture (Marissa)
Week 2 (load + stability): 30m canary at target throughput, scaling profile, and cold-start verification (Redwood infra)
Week 3 (validation + close): joint review, handoff artifacts to procurement, final signoff or rollback decision (stakeholders)

Acceptance heuristics (refined):
- Pass: core correctness >= 95% and no high-sev safety finding AND p95 < 500ms
- Conditional pass: correctness between 92-95% with documented remediation plan + p95 < 400ms
- Fail / stop: correctness < 92% or any high-sev safety finding or mean latency > 1s during canary

For the test-suite, I attached eval-test-scenarios.csv with concrete cases and expected outputs. Karthik — can you provide the quick tuning checklist (quantization, KV cache settings) we discussed?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min alignment call if helpful.

Tessa

Alex / team —

I've mapped the acceptance heuristics into a short checklist that we can run during each milestone. Attaching acceptance-checklist-v2.xlsx with a one-page pass/fail rubric. Highlights below so procurement has a quick read: 

1) Functional smoke (owner: Acme eng / validator: Redwood QA)
   - Trigger: 100 canonical prompts + 20 edge cases
   - Pass: recall >= 95% on canonical set AND <= 2 critical mismatches on edge cases
   - Evidence: signed CSV of inputs/outputs + scoring script output

2) Safety sweep (owner: Acme risk / validator: Redwood risk lead)
   - Trigger: 50 adversarial prompts + 50 PHI-check prompts
   - Pass: 0 high-sev hallucinations; medium-sev items documented and triaged
   - Evidence: labeled report and example traces with timestamps

3) Performance canary (owner: Redwood infra / validator: Acme eng)
   - Trigger: 30-minute sustained throughput at your target QPS
   - Pass: p95 < 500ms, error rate < 0.5%
   - Fallback: if p95 between 500ms–1s, run a tuning pass; if >1s stop and collect logs
4) Regression thresholding (owner: Marissa)
   - Any metric that regresses > 6ppt from baseline triggers a mandatory debrief and a targeted remediation sprint before we recommend capacity reservations.

Operational notes: 
- Test ownership: each test row has a named owner; we expect Acme to own the functional validation of domain-specific prompts.
- Artifacts: we will push scoring artifacts into the shared Drive folder.
- Signoff: final close requires procurement signoff + engineering acceptance.

If this looks good I can convert the checklist into a short runbook for the kickoff call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acceptance-checklist-v2.xlsx
